memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do nothing to the woman; she has committed no sin deserving death. This case is like that of someone who attacks and murders a neighbor, for the man found the young woman out in the country, and though the betrothed woman screamed, there was no one to rescue her. - Deut 22:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's law makes it wonderfully clear, "Do nothing to the woman; she has committed no sin deserving death." The victim of assault is declared innocent. God compares her situation to that of a murder victim, someone who was attacked and had no one to rescue her. Her cries went unheard by people, but they were not unheard by God. He knew she was helpless, and He counted her guiltless.

This is deeply tender. In the moment of her terror, "there was no one to rescue her." Yet God saw. He recorded her innocence in His law. Even when no human being came to her aid, God was not blind to her suffering or her helplessness. He is a God who sees the afflicted when no one else does.

What comfort this holds for anyone who has suffered when no one came to help. You may have cried out and felt utterly alone, thinking no one saw or cared. But God saw. He knows the difference between the guilty and the victim, and He holds no blame against those who were wronged. He is the God who sees the helpless and hears the cries that others miss (Ps 56:8). And in Jesus, God Himself entered our suffering world, drawing near to the abandoned and the broken. If you feel unseen in your pain, know that the God of the universe sees you fully and loves you tenderly. How does it comfort you to know that God sees even what others miss?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you that God sees your hidden pain?
2. Where have you felt that "no one came to rescue"?
3. How does God's nearness meet you in those places?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You see the helpless and hear the cries others miss. When I feel unseen and alone, remind me that You are near. Amen.
